gaps.sentence: She's ___ of winning a medal this season.
gaps.explanation: 'Be capable of doing' = have the ability/skill; 'able' needs 'able to do'.

gaps.sentence: I'm really ___ forward to the weekend.
gaps.explanation: 'Look forward to' is the fixed phrase; 'wait forward' does not exist.

gaps.sentence: The ancient manuscript was written ___ papyrus.
gaps.explanation: Text is written ON a physical surface (on paper, on papyrus); 'in ink' for the substance.

gaps.sentence: Her first novel was an ___ success.
gaps.explanation: 'An overnight success' = sudden success; 'overdue' = later than expected.

gaps.sentence: The plans for the new stadium were ___ when the funding fell through.
gaps.explanation: 'Scrap plans' = abandon them completely; 'scrape' means rub or just manage.

gaps.sentence: The singer was ___ greeted by thousands of fans.
gaps.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify 'greeted': enthusiastically.

gaps.sentence: We had to ___ the meeting short because of the alarm.
gaps.explanation: 'Cut something short' = end it earlier than planned.

gaps.sentence: The dustmen ___ our rubbish every Tuesday morning.
gaps.explanation: 'Collect the rubbish' is the standard phrase; pick would need 'up'.
